 Meet the Cast of Netflix’s The Blue Road , Led by Son Suk-ku
 Sweety High Staff 
 Nov 20, 2026
 Netflix ‘s Korea-Japan crime thriller The Blue Road is streaming now, with all eight episodes available as of Nov. 20. It pairs Son Suk-ku with Eita Nagayama as two detectives chasing the same killer.
 The series is rated TV-MA and follows a string of twisted murders across Korea, Japan and Hong Kong. Here is who is in the cast and who is behind the camera.
 ( The Blue Road  via Netflix)
 Premiere date: Nov. 20, with all eight episodes released together
 Where to watch: Netflix
 Cast: Son Suk-ku, Eita Nagayama, Kim Shin-rok, Choi Sung-eun and Jung Jae-young
 Director: Han Jun-hee
 Who Is in the Cast of The Blue Road ?
 Son Suk-ku leads the series as Kim Seok, a detective with the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency’s Mobile Investigation Unit.
 Eita Nagayama plays his Japanese counterpart, Inose Hiroshi, a detective with the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department.
 Kim Shin-rok, Choi Sung-eun and Jung Jae-young round out the main cast. 
 What Is The Blue Road About?
 The story begins with a string of bizarre murders. Netflix describes twisted bodies and mysterious messages left behind, with clues that cross borders.
 Kim Seok and Inose have to work together even though they speak different languages. The series is set in 2002 and is adapted from a comic.
 Both actors delivered lines in each other’s languages, and Son said they rehearsed with the help of an interpreter.
 A First Korean Project for Eita Nagayama
 This is Eita Nagayama’s first Korean project. He has built his career in Japanese film and television, including the film Monster .
 Son Suk-ku is no stranger to the genre. Fans will know him from A Killer Paradox and D.P. , and he reunites with the D.P. director here.
 The cast and director Han Jun-hee met the press in Seoul on Nov. 17, ahead of the premiere.
 Also read about: Lee Jae Wook’s Dead-End Job Is Now Streaming on Netflix 
 Who Is Behind the Camera?
 Han Jun-hee directs, and screenwriter Cho Yu-jin adapts the original comic for the screen.
 The first three episodes screened at the Busan International Film Festival in October, so some viewers have already had a head start.
 Is The Blue Road Worth a Binge?
 If you like slow-burn mysteries and odd-couple detective pairings, it looks like a good fit for a long weekend. With all eight episodes out together, you can finish the case in one go.
 Keep in mind the TV-MA rating, since the story deals with violent crimes.
